goal: lapa" is a general controller of the Windows desktop. It must reliably operate ANY window and ANY field in ANY app: perceive the screen, target the RIGHT element, act, and verify the REAL outcome. Telegram is ONLY a test surface - no app-specific APIs, no special-casing. Reliability strictly dominates coverage: a clean abort beats a wrong action. The goal is to PERMANENTLY and FULLY solve desktop control for the operator.
constraints: Must reliably operate ANY window and ANY field in ANY app.
No app-specific APIs or special-casing; Telegram is ONLY a test surface.
Reliability strictly dominates coverage; a clean abort beats a wrong action.
The solution must PERMANENTLY and FULLY solve desktop control for the operator.
Vision is perception-only, lazy (only on UIA-miss), single-call, and returns a selector REFINEMENT that must re-resolve and pass every gate; it NEVER clicks coordinates.
A safety risk-ladder must be implemented: low actions auto; send/delete/publish/buy -> confirm with the user; passwords/2FA/payment -> never.
A STOP hotkey must be implemented.
No reintroduction of blind escalation, blind coordinate-clicks, flag-based success, or app-special-casing.
known_context: - A dedicated long-lived STA worker thread that OWNS COM/UIA (fixed a cross-apartment segfault).
- Verify-or-abort by ELEMENT IDENTITY before acting (hit-test ElementFromPoint + focus check before any blind keystroke; never type into an unverified field).
- Verify success on REAL STATE (re-read the actual value / last message), never a success flag or a log line.
- Idempotency: read current state before acting; skip if already done (no duplicate sends).
- Fragile tiered escalation uia->vision->browser as a blind fallback chain (slow ~27s/run, each tier a new failure surface).
- Blind typing into "the active field/chat" without verifying identity (the root of wrong-contact and mistype).
- False-success (reporting done when nothing, or the wrong thing, happened).
- Over-layering / unpredictable complexity (the user explicitly called the old design fragile and one-sided).
- ONE deterministic loop, not a ladder.

- Five gates per action: PERCEIVE (one window-scoped UIA snapshot, generation-tagged) -> RESOLVE (a declarative selector to EXACTLY-ONE element, or abort - never first-match) -> PROVE (identity at the action point: live re-read + ElementFromPoint hit-test + focus assertion for keystrokes) -> ACT (via the element's own UIA pattern: SetValue/Invoke/Toggle/Select; keystrokes only as an identity+focus-gated last resort) -> VERIFY (real post-state read + foreground-context recheck).
- Vision is perception-only, lazy (only on a UIA-miss), single-call, and returns a selector REFINEMENT that must re-resolve and pass every gate - it NEVER clicks coordinates.

- Additions being folded in: app-launcher (open apps by system call, not by hunting an icon), window-manager (focus/move/resize by Win32 command), clipboard-paste for long text, a safety risk-ladder, a STOP hotkey, a task-contract in / evidence-report out, and a metrics+benchmark that PROVES reliability (tracking wrong-window-actions and irreversible-errors).
success_tests: The proposed solution demonstrably operates ANY window and ANY field in ANY app without app-specific APIs or special-casing.
Reliability metrics (e.g., wrong-window-actions, irreversible-errors) from the benchmark show near-zero critical failures.
The system consistently performs clean aborts instead of wrong actions when uncertainty is detected.
All 'PROVEN WINS' are verifiably maintained in the new design.
All 'BURNS' are structurally prevented and not reintroduced in any form.
The safety risk-ladder and STOP hotkey are fully implemented and function as specified.
The system achieves acceptable speed for common desktop automation tasks.
The proposed changes generalize across arbitrary applications without requiring app-specific hacks.
The solution provides a clear evidence-report for each task execution, detailing actions and verification steps.
